extracted.intended_audience: researchers, editors, publishers, and policy-makers interested in the study and reform of peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Identifying and describing criteria, topics, and standards for evaluating and researching journal-coupled peer review (including editors', reviewers' and authors' roles, openness, reproducibility, types of review, and social/epistemic impacts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility of research
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review should contribute to reproducibility, yet reviewers are often unable to physically reproduce experiments and inter-reviewer reliability is variable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise that reviewers typically must trust authors' methods; consider specialised reviewers (methods, statistics) and automated services (e.g. checking statistical analyses) to improve rigour. The review process should treat reproducibility not as a post hoc concern but as a formal requirement where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-reviewer reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which different reviewers produce consistent judgements about the same manuscript (one aspect of reproducibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing research shows variable results; this is a measurable topic for study and a determinant of review consistency and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency / openness of peer review (publishing review reports, open identities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Making review reports public and/or revealing reviewer identities as a form of increased transparency and rigour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opening reports may change reviewer behaviour (more critical or more lenient), affect acceptance to review, alter tone, length, substance, submission time, and incur costs. Publicised reports will be skewed toward ultimately published articles and may exclude rejected manuscripts' reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of editors in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors' functions in arbitration, quality control, reviewer selection, and encouraging community engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate how editors act, justify decisions, and how much editorial mediation is required for open or decoupled peer review systems; editorial practices shape reviewer uptake and quality control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justifications for editorial decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that editors provide reasons for accept/reject/other decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research should examine how and whether editors document and communicate justifications and the impact on perceived fairness and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors that affect editorial quality, impartiality and their impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Determinants of editorial competence and impartiality and consequences for the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study influences such as career incentives, conflicts, workload, and institutional context and how they affect decisions and downstream epistemic diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: How editors select reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial processes and criteria used to choose reviewers for manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine selection criteria, networks, and potential biases (centralisation, homogeneity) and their effects on review quality and diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of reviewer selection on relationships with editors and authors
rubrics_metrics.description: How reviewer choices influence social relationships and editorial-author dynamics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is considered difficult to study but important; investigate whether reviewer selection affects trust, conflicts, and future interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial competencies and motivations for decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Skills, knowledge, and incentives that drive editorial decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and assess core competencies for editors and motivations (career, reputation) that may shape decisions; consider training or core competency standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of decisions on epistemic diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: How editorial and review decisions shape the diversity of ideas and perspectives represented in the literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether decisions lead to conservatism or suppression of innovation and the consequences for replicability and scientific progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial conflicts of interest and relationships with other parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification and declaration of editors' conflicts of interest and their relationships (with authors, publishers, funders).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research and policy should focus on declaration practices and their enforcement; authors recommend declaring editorial conflicts and documenting misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent of editorial misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The prevalence and nature of editorial malpractice or inappropriate behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical work is needed to document misconduct and its impact; detection depends on access to editorial records and openness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence of reviewer recommendations on editorial decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree to which editors follow, weigh, or disregard reviewer recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study the 'invisible hand' of reviewer recommendations and how much editorial discretion modifies or overrides those recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of editors’ careers on their scientific career
rubrics_metrics.description: How editorial roles influence editors' own career trajectories and incentives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine potential conflicts where editorial decisions may be affected by personal career considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of reviewers in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers' responsibilities, behaviours, and influence on the peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics include impartiality, competencies, motivations, and how reviewer actions feed into editorial decisions and the scholarly record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors that affect reviewer impartiality and their impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Determinants of bias or partiality in reviewers and the consequences for fairness and quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes social, cognitive, and institutional drivers; assess methods to mitigate bias (blinding, training, disclosure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conflicts of interest and relationships with other parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial, professional, or personal ties that may compromise reviewer judgement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study prevalence, disclosure practices, and effects on recommendations and editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer competencies and motivations
rubrics_metrics.description: The skills and incentives reviewers bring to review tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define expectations and potential core competencies; investigate how motivations (altruism, reputation, career) affect review quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors that affect inter-reviewer reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Determinants of agreement or disagreement among multiple reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirically measurable (e.g., multilevel meta-analyses); important for assessing consistency of peer review across disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent of peer review misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Prevalence of unethical behaviours by reviewers (e.g., stealing ideas, sabotage, inappropriate confidentiality breaches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires empirical investigation and mechanisms for detection, reporting, and remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: What reviewers are expected to do (e.g., assess rigour, reproducibility, novelty, clarity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify and possibly standardise reviewer expectations across journals and disciplines to improve consistency and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of incentives for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: How rewards or recognition (or lack thereof) affect reviewers' willingness to participate and quality of reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate which incentive structures (credits, acknowledgement, formal evaluation) increase uptake and performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformation of reviewers to journal policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which reviewers follow and enforce specific journal policies (ethics, data sharing, reporting standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine compliance and the role of editors in ensuring reviewers align with policy expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent to which anonymity is compromised
rubrics_metrics.description: How often reviewer anonymity is unintentionally or intentionally revealed and the implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study mechanisms that lead to de-anonymisation and consequences for reviewer behaviour and safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: How notions of expertise affect reviewer behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: The role that perceived or actual expertise plays in reviewer selection and evaluation practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess definitions of expertise, their validity, and how they influence judgements and epistemic diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of reviewing on scientific careers of reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: How participating in peer review affects reviewers' own research careers and professional standing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate career benefits or harms, and whether review activity should be formally valued in hiring/promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of authors in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors' interactions with (and influence on) the peer review process, including recommendations and responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study effects of author-suggested reviewers, responses to reviews, and how authors' actions shape review outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of author recommendations on reviews and reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: How author-provided reviewer suggestions affect the review process and reviewer decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine biases introduced by author recommendations (networks, conflicts) and editorial safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functionality and quality of peer review (what peer review actually is and does)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify the fundamental functions of peer review (improving manuscripts vs. gatekeeping) and evaluate effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research should disentangle peer review's multiple functions and measure outcomes relevant to each.

rubrics_metrics.name: How peer review impacts scientific discourse
rubrics_metrics.description: Effects of peer review on the development, dissemination, and framing of scientific ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study peer review's influence on what gets published, cited, and built upon in scholarly conversation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship between peer review and journal quality
rubrics_metrics.description: How peer review practices correlate with measures of journal quality and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate whether journal metrics (e.g., impact factor) reflect the rigor of peer review and editorial standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cases where peer review is redundant
rubrics_metrics.description: Situations in which peer review may not add value (e.g., certain preprint or post-publication contexts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine trade-offs between rapid dissemination and critical assessment to identify contexts where peer review could be scaled or omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether peer review decisions and processes are themselves reproducible when repeated or audited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate processes and metrics to measure reproducibility of review outcomes and interventional changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development and impact of peer review standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Creation, adoption, and effects of standards for reviewing and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend a minimal set of criteria for standards and reporting and shared infrastructures for data to enable comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homogeneity and centralisation of reviewer pools
rubrics_metrics.description: The concentration of reviewer networks and lack of epistemic diversity resulting from centralised, homogeneous reviewer communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how reviewer pool composition affects inclusivity, bias, and the range of accepted viewpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Epistemic diversity of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Diversity of perspectives, methods, and assumptions represented in reviewers and editorial choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure excluded opinions and consequences of epistemic exclusion; aim to mitigate harmful homogeneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of peer review on innovation or conservatism
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether peer review encourages conservative, incremental work over innovative, risky research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine the trade-off between creativity/originality and consensus/rigour and locate optimal balance points for different fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review as a vehicle for disseminating prestige
rubrics_metrics.description: Role of peer review and journals in distributing academic capital and standing across communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine whether peer review functions to gatekeep prestige and how that shapes research trajectories and access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors influencing the choice of peer review type
rubrics_metrics.description: Determinants (logistical, cultural, disciplinary) behind choosing single-blind, double-blind, open, interactive, or post-publication review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study practical and normative trade-offs, including costs, quality control, and participant preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence of peer review type on quality of review and potential misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: How different review models affect review quality, error detection, and opportunities for misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirically compare models (e.g., interactive vs. traditional) for outcomes like error detection rates, speed, and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do micro-publications impact reviewer engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether smaller, quicker publication formats increase reviewer uptake and participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess assumptions that micro-publications lower time burden and thus increase engagement; test effects empirically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is interactive peer review more effective
rubrics_metrics.description: Effectiveness of interactive (editorially controlled discussions between reviewers and authors) versus traditional unilateral exchanges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure review quality, error detection rates, turnaround time, and cost implications of interactive processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: How have/will preprints impact peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Effects of preprint dissemination on conventional peer review cycles, speed, and public commenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study uptake of overlay services, preprint-based review platforms, and whether preprints alter the need for or function of journal peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are overlay journals/services more effective
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether overlay review services (review/comment layers on preprints) provide effective alternatives to journal-coupled review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate sustainability, impact on publication fate, and whether authors view overlay review as sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which OPR services do researchers prefer
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferences among researchers for different open peer review systems (journal-run or third-party).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey across disciplines to identify favored systems and features; explore factors that encourage uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: What measures can incentivise OPR
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies or incentives that would increase adoption of open peer review practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider recognition, credit, reducing burdens, editorial encouragement, and integration into reward structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researcher attitudes towards OPR for non-traditional outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: How researchers view open peer review applied to outputs beyond journal articles (data, software, proposals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirically examine attitudes across disciplines and output types; question transferability of article-oriented norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: The impact of OPR on participant diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: How openness affects demographic and disciplinary participation among authors, editors, and reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether open models increase or decrease inclusivity and whether certain groups are deterred by openness.

rubrics_metrics.name: The impact of blinding on biases and review quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Effects of anonymisation (single/double-blind) on bias reduction and review outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study whether blinding reduces demographic/prestige biases and how it affects error detection and reviewer behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of open review reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Consequences of publishing review reports on reviewer behaviour, editorial processes, and the scholarly record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider both potential increases in criticality and potential chilling effects; evidence shows mixed outcomes and needs further study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of review type on careers of reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: How different review models (open vs anonymous, interactive vs unilateral) influence reviewers' career outcomes and reputational effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine whether reviewers gain recognition or experience career risks from different review transparency regimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of editorial conflicts of interests and documenting any editorial misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to require editors to declare conflicts and to report/document any instances of editorial misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-priority action for immediate progress; transparency mechanisms should be implemented and studied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Studies as a discrete multidisciplinary field
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish peer review studies combining social sciences, history, philosophy, scientometrics, network analysis, psychology, library studies, and journalology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create sustained multidisciplinary research programmes with funding, shared infrastructure, and common vocabulary/standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define a minimum standard for what constitutes peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Reach global consensus and define core elements of peer review as a boundary object accommodating field-specific variations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for a minimal standard to facilitate comparability while allowing disciplinary differences; useful for infrastructure and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full systematic review of global knowledge pool of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct comprehensive systematic reviews to map existing evidence and identify knowledge gaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the outputs to quantitatively demarcate gaps and prioritise future empirical work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint infrastructure for data sharing and minimal reporting criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Create shared open data infrastructure built around a minimal set of criteria for standards and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential for enabling reproducible, comparable peer review research and for assessing the efficacy/value added by peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design a core outcome set for peer review research
rubrics_metrics.description: Define standard outcomes to be measured across studies of peer review to optimise comparability and effectiveness assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A core outcome set would streamline research, enable meta-analyses, and guide policy and practice changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish baseline knowledge and core competencies for reviewers and editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulate baseline skills and competencies required to perform peer review and editorial duties appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use competency frameworks to inform training, evaluation, and incentives; aligns with calls for core competencies for scientific editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuing peer review in hiring, promotion and tenure
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognise and reward peer review activity in institutional assessments to incentivise high-quality review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate peer review contributions into career evaluation to motivate proper engagement, especially for early-career researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost, time and efficiency of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantify human time, financial costs, and inefficiencies (e.g., reject–resubmit cycles) associated with peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform cost–benefit analyses comparing quality control benefits to time/costs; existing estimates suggest large human-time values and wasted hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of automated services in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential role of automated tools (e.g., statistical checks) to assist reviewers in quality assurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automation may improve reproducibility but raises questions about the role of human reviewers and integration into editorial workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public record skew and selection effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Awareness that publicised review reports are biased toward published articles and may omit reviews for rejected/unpublished work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing open review impacts, account for selection biases in the publicly visible corpus of reviews.
